title: PRD ambiguity triage runway & owner matrix
creator: Sofia Gomez
description: Goal: Remove ambiguous acceptance conditions from the PRD for the Structured Output pilot and create a concrete triage runway and owner matrix so engineering, design, and legal can sign off independently and in parallel where possible. Background: recent PRD drafts for the Structured Output work surfaced 6 ambiguous decision points (data retention, fallback UX, error taxonomy, model variant pinning, observable telemetry surface, export controls). Those ambiguities are blocking scope decisions and preventing safe canary rollouts. This ticket coordinates the cross-team process: 1) run a fast ambiguity triage meeting; 2) assign explicit decision owners and SLAs for each ambiguity; 3) document precise acceptance criteria; 4) produce a sign-off checklist and automation (GitHub checklist + Console gating flag). Outcome: PRD is acceptance-ready for release to engineering backlog and Dedicated pilot without open legal or security blockers.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 previously-identified ambiguity items have a single named owner (PM/Eng/Design/Legal) and a deadline.
Each ambiguity has a one-line decision, the rationale, and the roll-forward plan recorded in the PRD Confluence page.
Design has provided annotated mocks for fallback states and error copy for the two highest-risk flows.
Engineering has produced one-line feasibility notes for any scope reductions and a rough estimate for the minimal viable rollout (MVR).
Legal has confirmed the data residency and export-control constraints or produced required contract language and a mitigation plan.
An automated PR checklist (GitHub template) that gates merge to the release branch is added and referenced in the PRD.
Telemetry owner has a draft dashboard and a burn-rate alert threshold defined for the canary phase.
Updated PRD link is posted in the console-acceptance Slack channel with an explicit acceptance stamp from PM/Eng/Design/Legal.
No open 'high' legal/security items remain; if any remain they must be labelled and escalated with an explicit timeline.
Updated_at date on the PRD reflects the final acceptance update before the release cutoff date (2026-03-31).

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Legal export-control findings delay canary — Mitigation: remove EU export flows from MVR and plan a separate controlled pilot.
Risk: Eng identifies unanticipated perf regression due to KV cache interactions — Mitigation: require perf smoke test and fallback to smaller context length for canary.
Risk: Design not accepted by PM leading to rework — Mitigation: fast iteration loop with 2-hour sync and explicit acceptance checklist.
Risk: Missing telemetry during canary — Mitigation: telemetry owner must provide dashboard and alert before any canary traffic; block rollout otherwise.
Risk: Security review uncovers KMS integration gaps — Mitigation: add security gating and schedule immediate remediation sprint prior to dedicated rollout.
